source.text: וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת אֵ֗לֶּה נִגְּשׁ֨וּ אֵלַ֤י הַשָּׂרִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־נִבְדְּל֞וּ הָעָ֤ם יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מֵעַמֵּ֖י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת כְּ֠תוֹעֲבֹֽתֵיהֶם לַכְּנַעֲנִ֨י הַחִתִּ֜י הַפְּרִזִּ֣י הַיְבוּסִ֗י הָֽעַמֹּנִי֙ הַמֹּ֣אָבִ֔י הַמִּצְרִ֖י וְהָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And when were finished these [things], drew near to me the princes, saying, Not have separated themselves the people Israel and the priests and the Levites from [the] peoples of the lands, according to their abominations, to the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, the Moabite, the Egyptian, and the Amorite;

en.L: And when these [things] were finished, the princes drew near to me, saying, "The people [of] Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, according to their abominations, [those] of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites;
en.B: After these things had been done, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites among them, have not kept themselves separate from the peoples of the lands and their detestable practices, the practices of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.
en.R: When all this was done, the leaders came to me. They said, "The people of Israel, even the priests and the Levites, have not kept themselves apart from the people living in the land. Those peoples do disgusting things, like the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

es.L: Y cuando estas [cosas] fueron terminadas, se acercaron a mí los príncipes, diciendo: «El pueblo [de] Israel y los sacerdotes y los levitas no se han separado de los pueblos de las tierras, conforme a sus abominaciones, [las] de los cananeos, los hititas, los ferezeos, los jebuseos, los amonitas, los moabitas, los egipcios y los amorreos;
es.B: Después de que se hicieron estas cosas, los jefes vinieron a mí y me dijeron: «El pueblo de Israel, y entre ellos los sacerdotes y los levitas, no se han mantenido separados de los pueblos de las tierras y de sus prácticas detestables, las prácticas de los cananeos, hititas, ferezeos, jebuseos, amonitas, moabitas, egipcios y amorreos.
es.R: Cuando todo esto terminó, los jefes vinieron a verme. Me dijeron: «El pueblo de Israel, y aun los sacerdotes y los levitas, no se han mantenido apartados de la gente que vive en el país. Esos pueblos hacen cosas repugnantes, como los cananeos, los hititas, los ferezeos, los jebuseos, los amonitas, los moabitas, los egipcios y los amorreos.

fr.L: Et quand ces [choses] furent achevées, les princes s’approchèrent de moi en disant : « Le peuple d’Israël, et les prêtres et les Lévites ne se sont pas séparés des peuples des pays, selon leurs abominations, [celles] des Cananéens, des Hittites, des Phéréziens, des Jébusiens, des Ammonites, des Moabites, des Égyptiens et des Amoréens ;
fr.B: Après cela, les chefs vinrent me trouver et me dirent : « Le peuple d’Israël, avec les prêtres et les Lévites, ne s’est pas tenu séparé des peuples des pays et de leurs pratiques abominables, celles des Cananéens, des Hittites, des Phéréziens, des Jébusiens, des Ammonites, des Moabites, des Égyptiens et des Amoréens.
fr.R: Quand tout cela a été fait, les chefs sont venus me trouver. Ils m’ont dit : « Le peuple d’Israël, et même les prêtres et les Lévites, n’est pas resté à l’écart des gens qui habitent dans le pays. Ces peuples font des choses horribles, comme les Cananéens, les Hittites, les Phéréziens, les Jébusiens, les Ammonites, les Moabites, les Égyptiens et les Amoréens.

sw.L: Na mambo hayo yalipokwisha, wakuu wakanikaribia, wakisema, "Watu [wa] Israeli na makuhani na Walawi hawajajitenga na mataifa ya nchi, kwa machukizo yao, [yale] ya Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waperizi, Wayebusi, Waamoni, Wamoabu, Wamisri, na Waamori;
sw.B: Baada ya mambo hayo kufanyika, viongozi walinijia, wakasema, "Watu wa Israeli, pamoja na makuhani na Walawi walio kati yao, hawajajitenga na mataifa ya nchi na desturi zao za kuchukiza, desturi za Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waperizi, Wayebusi, Waamoni, Wamoabu, Wamisri na Waamori.
sw.R: Mambo hayo yote yalipokwisha, viongozi walinijia. Wakasema, "Watu wa Israeli, hata makuhani na Walawi, hawajajitenga na watu walioishi katika nchi. Mataifa hayo hufanya mambo ya kuchukiza, kama Wakanaani, Wahiti, Waperizi, Wayebusi, Waamoni, Wamoabu, Wamisri na Waamori.

vi.L: Và khi những [việc] này đã xong, các quan trưởng đến gần tôi mà nói: "Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, các thầy tế lễ và người Lê-vi đã không tách mình ra khỏi các dân của các xứ, theo những điều ghê tởm của họ, [những điều] của người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Giê-bu-sít, người Am-môn, người Mô-áp, người Ai Cập và người A-mô-rít;
vi.B: Sau khi những việc ấy đã xong, các vị lãnh đạo đến gặp tôi và nói: "Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, kể cả các thầy tế lễ và người Lê-vi, đã không giữ mình tách biệt khỏi các dân của các xứ và những thói tục ghê tởm của họ, là thói tục của người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Giê-bu-sít, người Am-môn, người Mô-áp, người Ai Cập và người A-mô-rít.
vi.R: Khi mọi việc ấy đã xong, các vị lãnh đạo đến gặp tôi. Họ nói: "Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, ngay cả các thầy tế lễ và người Lê-vi, đã không giữ mình cách biệt với những dân đang sống trong xứ. Những dân ấy làm những điều gớm ghiếc, giống như người Ca-na-an, người Hê-tít, người Phê-rê-sít, người Giê-bu-sít, người Am-môn, người Mô-áp, người Ai Cập và người A-mô-rít.

decisions.choice: when these things were finished: after the gifts were handed over and the offerings made (8:33-36); Ezra tells it in the first person
decisions.reason: "These things" points back to the end of chapter 8, where the silver and gold were weighed out at the temple, the returned exiles offered sacrifices, and the king's orders were delivered to the governors. Ezra had arrived in the fifth month (7:9) and the assembly of 10:9 meets in the ninth, so the report comes some weeks or months after his arrival. As since 7:27, Ezra speaks of himself as "I" and "me".

decisions.choice: have not separated themselves: have not kept apart from the other peoples as a people set apart to God
decisions.reason: The verb means to divide or set apart. It is used of God setting Israel apart from the peoples to be his own (Leviticus 20:24, 26), and in this book of those who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the nations to keep the Passover (6:21). The complaint is about marriage, as verse 2 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: the list of peoples: the nations of the law's warnings against intermarriage
decisions.reason: The list joins the peoples of Canaan whom Israel was forbidden to marry (Exodus 34:11-16; Deuteronomy 7:1-4) with the Ammonites and Moabites, who were barred from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:4), and the Egyptians (Deuteronomy 23:8-9). It describes the peoples around Judah in the terms the law used, so that the leaders' complaint is heard as a breach of those commands.

decisions.choice: according to their abominations, to the Canaanites ...: the detestable practices of the peoples of the lands, like those of the Canaanites and the rest
alternatives: have not separated themselves from the Canaanites, the Hittites ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the list to "their abominations" with a small word meaning "to" or "as to". It most likely says whose abominations these are like: the peoples of the lands do what the old nations of Canaan did. It can also be read as naming the peoples Israel failed to separate from.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal), leaders (Balanced, Readable); abominations (Literal), detestable practices (Balanced), disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for "prince" is rendered "leaders" at Balanced here because 9:2 sets it beside another word, rendered "officials", and these men are the heads of the community (10:8, 14). "Abomination" names what is hateful to God, mostly false worship and its practices; Balanced and Readable say what it is in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L), "jefes" (B, R); "abominaciones" (L), "prácticas detestables" (B), "cosas repugnantes" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the word for princes is "jefes" at Balanced and Readable, since verse 2 sets it beside "funcionarios"; Balanced and Readable say what the abominations are in everyday words. The peoples are named in their published Spanish forms.

decisions.choice: "wakuu" (L), "viongozi" (B, R); "machukizo" (L), "desturi za kuchukiza" (B), "mambo ya kuchukiza" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Balanced calls these heads of the community "leaders" so they stay apart from the "maafisa" of verse 2; the abominations are named in everyday words below Literal.

decisions.choice: "princes" (Literal), "chefs" (Balanced, Readable); "abominations" (Literal), "pratiques abominables" (Balanced), "choses horribles" (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the English: Balanced and Readable call these men "chefs", to keep them apart from the "officials" of verse 2. The peoples keep the French forms of Deuteronomy 7:1.

decisions.choice: các quan trưởng (Literal), các vị lãnh đạo (Balanced, Readable); những điều ghê tởm (Literal), những thói tục ghê tởm (Balanced), những điều gớm ghiếc (Readable)
decisions.reason: The leaders are worded as the English does here, since verse 2 sets "các quan trưởng / các vị lãnh đạo" beside "các quan chức". The abominations are the peoples' detestable practices (m4).

source.text: כִּֽי־נָשְׂא֣וּ מִבְּנֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם לָהֶם֙ וְלִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְהִתְעָֽרְבוּ֙ זֶ֣רַע הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ בְּעַמֵּ֖י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְיַ֧ד הַשָּׂרִ֣ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֗ים הָֽיְתָ֛ה בַּמַּ֥עַל הַזֶּ֖ה רִאשׁוֹנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For they have taken from their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and have mixed themselves the seed of holiness with [the] peoples of the lands; and [the] hand of the princes and the officials has been in this unfaithfulness first.

en.L: for they have taken [some] of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed has mixed itself with the peoples of the lands; and the hand of the princes and the officials has been first in this unfaithfulness."
en.B: They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy race has mingled with the peoples of the lands. And the leaders and officials have led the way in this unfaithfulness."
en.R: Some of our men have married women from these peoples, and they have let their sons marry them too. So God's holy people have mixed with the people living in the land. And the leaders and officials were the first to be unfaithful in this way."

es.L: porque han tomado de sus hijas para sí y para sus hijos, y la descendencia santa se ha mezclado con los pueblos de las tierras; y la mano de los príncipes y de los oficiales ha sido la primera en esta infidelidad».
es.B: Han tomado a algunas de sus hijas como esposas para sí mismos y para sus hijos, de modo que el linaje santo se ha mezclado con los pueblos de las tierras. Y los jefes y los funcionarios han sido los primeros en esta infidelidad».
es.R: Algunos de nuestros hombres se han casado con mujeres de esos pueblos, y también han dejado que sus hijos se casen con ellas. Así el pueblo santo de Dios se ha mezclado con la gente que vive en el país. Y los jefes y los funcionarios fueron los primeros en ser infieles de esta manera».

fr.L: car ils ont pris de leurs filles pour eux et pour leurs fils, et la semence sainte s’est mêlée aux peuples des pays ; et la main des princes et des magistrats a été la première dans cette infidélité. »
fr.B: Ils ont pris de leurs filles pour épouses, pour eux et pour leurs fils, de sorte que la race sainte s’est mêlée aux peuples des pays. Et les chefs et les magistrats ont été les premiers dans cette infidélité. »
fr.R: Certains de nos hommes ont épousé des femmes de ces peuples, et ils ont laissé leurs fils les épouser aussi. Ainsi, le peuple saint de Dieu s’est mélangé aux gens qui habitent dans le pays. Et les chefs et les responsables ont été les premiers à être infidèles de cette façon. »

sw.L: kwa maana wamejitwalia binti zao kwa ajili yao wenyewe na kwa ajili ya wana wao, na uzao mtakatifu umejichanganya na mataifa ya nchi; na mkono wa wakuu na maafisa umekuwa wa kwanza katika uasi huu."
sw.B: Wamewaoa baadhi ya binti zao, wao wenyewe na wana wao, hata ukoo mtakatifu umechanganyika na mataifa ya nchi. Tena viongozi na maafisa wametangulia katika ukosefu huu wa uaminifu."
sw.R: Baadhi ya wanaume wetu wameoa wanawake kutoka mataifa hayo, na wamewaacha wana wao wawaoe pia. Hivyo watu watakatifu wa Mungu wamechanganyika na watu walioishi katika nchi. Tena viongozi na maafisa ndio waliokuwa wa kwanza kukosa uaminifu kwa namna hii."

vi.L: vì họ đã cưới [một số] con gái của những dân ấy cho chính mình và cho con trai mình, và dòng giống thánh đã pha trộn với các dân của các xứ; và tay của các quan trưởng và các quan chức đã đi đầu trong sự bất trung này."
vi.B: Họ đã cưới con gái của những dân ấy làm vợ cho mình và cho con trai mình, khiến dòng giống thánh bị pha trộn với các dân của các xứ. Các vị lãnh đạo và các quan chức lại đi đầu trong sự bất trung này."
vi.R: Một số người của chúng ta đã cưới phụ nữ thuộc các dân ấy, và còn để cho con trai mình cưới họ nữa. Vì vậy dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời đã pha trộn với những dân sống trong xứ. Mà các vị lãnh đạo và các quan chức lại là những người đầu tiên bất trung như thế."

decisions.choice: they have taken their daughters for themselves and for their sons: they have married them, and arranged their sons' marriages with them
decisions.reason: To "take" a woman "for" a man is the usual Hebrew way of saying he married her (Genesis 24:4; Deuteronomy 7:3). Fathers arranged marriages for their sons, so the fathers are named as responsible for both.

decisions.choice: the holy seed: Israel as a people set apart to God, whose families were not to be joined to the peoples around them
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring or descendants. Israel is called a holy people, set apart to God (Exodus 19:6; Deuteronomy 7:6), and Isaiah calls the surviving stump of Israel "holy seed" (Isaiah 6:13). The concern of the law was that marriage with the nations would turn Israel to their gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4; 1 Kings 11:1-8); the leaders see the same danger here.

decisions.choice: unfaithfulness: a breach of trust against God
decisions.reason: The word is used for acting faithlessly toward God, taking or doing what violates what is his (Leviticus 5:15; Joshua 7:1). It becomes the key word of chapters 9-10 (9:4; 10:2, 6, 10).

decisions.choice: the hand of the princes and officials has been first: the leaders have led the way
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for action and responsibility. Those who should have guarded the people were the first to do this, and the list in 10:18-44 begins with priests.

decisions.choice: the holy seed (Literal), the holy race (Balanced), God's holy people (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the book-wide choices for this phrase. "Seed" is kept at Literal; Balanced says "race" in the sense of a line of descent; Readable says plainly who is meant.

decisions.choice: princes and officials (Literal), leaders and officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The second word names lower officials or deputies and is rendered "officials" as in Nehemiah; to keep the two apart, Balanced and Readable call the first group "leaders".

decisions.choice: "la descendencia santa" (L); "el linaje santo" (B); "el pueblo santo de Dios" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for the holy seed: Literal keeps "descendencia" for "seed", Balanced says "linaje", a line of descent, and Readable says who is meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "uzao mtakatifu" (L), "ukoo mtakatifu" (B), "watu watakatifu wa Mungu" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the holy seed: Literal keeps "seed", Balanced a line of descent, Readable says who is meant.

decisions.choice: "uasi huu" (L); "ukosefu huu wa uaminifu" (B); "kukosa uaminifu" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is breaking faith with God; Balanced and Readable say so plainly, as the English "unfaithfulness" does.

decisions.choice: "la semence sainte" (Literal); "la race sainte" (Balanced); "le peuple saint de Dieu" (Readable)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the English term list: Literal keeps "semence", Balanced says "race" in the sense of a line of descent, Readable says who is meant.

decisions.choice: "infidélité"
decisions.reason: The key word of chapters 9-10, a breach of faith against God, is "infidélité" (Literal, Balanced) and "être infidèle" (Readable) throughout.

decisions.choice: dòng giống thánh (Literal, Balanced); dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The holy seed" is Israel as a people set apart to God (m2): Literal and Balanced say "dòng giống thánh", Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: sự bất trung (Literal, Balanced); bất trung (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word (*maʿal*) is a breach of faith against God (m3), so it is "bất trung" (unfaithfulness) at every level through chapters 9 and 10, not the general word for sin.

source.text: וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה קָרַ֥עְתִּי אֶת־בִּגְדִ֖י וּמְעִילִ֑י וָאֶמְרְטָ֞ה מִשְּׂעַ֤ר רֹאשִׁי֙ וּזְקָנִ֔י וָאֵשְׁבָ֖ה מְשׁוֹמֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And when I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled out [some] of [the] hair of my head and my beard, and sat appalled.

en.L: And when I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled out [some] of the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat down appalled.
en.B: When I heard this, I tore my tunic and my cloak, pulled out hair from my head and my beard, and sat down, stunned.
en.R: When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my coat. I pulled out some of the hair from my head and my beard. Then I sat down in shock.

es.L: Y cuando oí esto, rasgué mi vestido y mi manto, y me arranqué [parte] del pelo de mi cabeza y de mi barba, y me senté consternado.
es.B: Cuando oí esto, rasgué mi túnica y mi manto, me arranqué pelo de la cabeza y de la barba, y me senté, aturdido.
es.R: Cuando oí esto, rasgué mi ropa y mi manto. Me arranqué parte del pelo de la cabeza y de la barba. Luego me senté, impactado.

fr.L: Et quand j’entendis cette chose, je déchirai mon vêtement et mon manteau, et je m’arrachai [des] cheveux de ma tête et [des poils] de ma barbe, et je m’assis consterné.
fr.B: Quand j’entendis cela, je déchirai ma tunique et mon manteau, je m’arrachai des cheveux et des poils de la barbe, et je m’assis, accablé.
fr.R: Quand j’ai entendu cela, j’ai déchiré mes vêtements et mon manteau. Je me suis arraché des cheveux et des poils de barbe. Puis je me suis assis, sous le choc.

sw.L: Na niliposikia jambo hili, nikararua vazi langu na joho langu, nikang'oa [baadhi ya] nywele za kichwa changu na za ndevu zangu, nikaketi nimeduwaa.
sw.B: Niliposikia jambo hili, nilirarua kanzu yangu na joho langu, nikang'oa nywele za kichwa changu na ndevu zangu, nikaketi nimeshtuka.
sw.R: Niliposikia jambo hili, nilirarua nguo zangu na koti langu. Nikang'oa baadhi ya nywele za kichwa changu na za ndevu zangu. Kisha nikaketi chini nimeshtuka sana.

vi.L: Và khi tôi nghe điều này, tôi xé áo trong và áo choàng của tôi, nhổ [một ít] tóc trên đầu và râu của tôi, và ngồi xuống sững sờ.
vi.B: Khi tôi nghe điều ấy, tôi xé áo trong và áo choàng mình, nhổ tóc trên đầu và râu mình, rồi ngồi xuống, bàng hoàng.
vi.R: Khi nghe điều ấy, tôi xé áo trong và áo ngoài của mình. Tôi nhổ một ít tóc trên đầu và râu của mình. Rồi tôi ngồi xuống, sững sờ.

decisions.choice: tearing clothes and pulling out hair: signs of grief and horror
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the common sign of grief or dismay (Genesis 37:34; 2 Kings 22:11). Pulling out one's own hair and beard is stronger and is rare in Scripture; it shows how deeply Ezra was shaken. Compare Nehemiah, who pulled out the hair of the offenders instead (Nehemiah 13:25).

decisions.choice: appalled: stunned and desolate
decisions.reason: The word is related to the verb used of a land laid waste. It describes someone so shocked that he sits silent and unable to act (Daniel 8:27 uses the same verb). He sits like this until evening (verse 4).

decisions.choice: garment and robe: the garment worn underneath and the outer robe
decisions.reason: The second word is a robe or mantle, worn by priests and men of standing (1 Samuel 15:27; 18:4). Ezra tears both, the inner and the outer clothing.

decisions.choice: tunic and cloak (Balanced), clothes and coat (Readable); stunned, in shock
decisions.reason: Balanced names the two garments in familiar words; Readable keeps that there were two. "Appalled" is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable describe his state.

source.text: וְאֵלַ֣י יֵאָסְפ֗וּ כֹּ֤ל חָרֵד֙ בְּדִבְרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ל מַ֣עַל הַגּוֹלָ֑ה וַאֲנִי֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב מְשׁוֹמֵ֔ם עַ֖ד לְמִנְחַ֥ת הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And to me gathered everyone trembling at [the] words of [the] God of Israel over the unfaithfulness of the exile, and I [was] sitting appalled until the offering of the evening.

en.L: And to me gathered everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel, because of the unfaithfulness of the exile, while I sat appalled until the evening offering.
en.B: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles, while I sat there stunned until the evening offering.
en.R: Everyone who took seriously what the God of Israel had said came and gathered around me, because the people who came back from exile had been unfaithful. I sat there in shock until the time of the evening offering.

es.L: Y se reunieron conmigo todos los que temblaban ante las palabras del Dios de Israel, a causa de la infidelidad del destierro, mientras yo estaba sentado consternado hasta la ofrenda de la tarde.
es.B: Entonces todos los que temblaban ante las palabras del Dios de Israel se reunieron a mi alrededor a causa de la infidelidad de los que habían vuelto del destierro, mientras yo seguía sentado, aturdido, hasta la ofrenda de la tarde.
es.R: Todos los que tomaban en serio lo que el Dios de Israel había dicho vinieron y se reunieron a mi alrededor, porque los que regresaron del destierro habían sido infieles. Yo me quedé sentado, impactado, hasta la hora de la ofrenda de la tarde.

fr.L: Et auprès de moi se rassemblèrent tous ceux qui tremblaient aux paroles du Dieu d’Israël, à cause de l’infidélité de l’exil, tandis que j’étais assis, consterné, jusqu’à l’offrande du soir.
fr.B: Alors tous ceux qui tremblaient devant les paroles du Dieu d’Israël se rassemblèrent autour de moi, à cause de l’infidélité des exilés revenus, tandis que je restais assis, accablé, jusqu’à l’offrande du soir.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui prenaient au sérieux ce que le Dieu d’Israël avait dit sont venus se rassembler autour de moi, parce que les gens revenus de l’exil avaient été infidèles. Je suis resté assis, sous le choc, jusqu’au moment de l’offrande du soir.

sw.L: Na kwangu wakakusanyika kila mmoja aliyetetemeka kwa maneno ya Mungu wa Israeli, kwa sababu ya uasi wa uhamisho, nami nikaketi nimeduwaa mpaka sadaka ya jioni.
sw.B: Ndipo kila mtu aliyetetemeka kwa maneno ya Mungu wa Israeli akakusanyika kwangu kwa sababu ya ukosefu wa uaminifu wa waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni, nami nikaketi pale nimeshtuka mpaka wakati wa sadaka ya jioni.
sw.R: Kila mtu aliyeyachukua kwa uzito maneno ya Mungu wa Israeli alikuja na kukusanyika kwangu, kwa sababu watu waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni walikuwa wamekosa uaminifu. Nami nikaketi pale nimeshtuka mpaka wakati wa sadaka ya jioni.

vi.L: Và mọi người run sợ trước lời của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên nhóm lại với tôi, vì sự bất trung của những người lưu đày, trong khi tôi ngồi sững sờ cho đến lúc dâng tế lễ buổi chiều.
vi.B: Bấy giờ mọi người run sợ trước lời của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên tụ họp quanh tôi, vì sự bất trung của những người lưu đày trở về, trong khi tôi ngồi đó bàng hoàng cho đến lúc dâng tế lễ buổi chiều.
vi.R: Tất cả những ai kính sợ lời Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đều đến tụ họp quanh tôi, vì những người từ chốn lưu đày trở về đã bất trung. Tôi ngồi đó sững sờ cho đến giờ dâng tế lễ buổi chiều.

decisions.choice: everyone who trembled at the words of God: those who feared to disobey what God had said
decisions.reason: To tremble at God's word is to take it with reverent fear and dread breaking it (Isaiah 66:2, 5). The same people support Ezra's plan in 10:3.

decisions.choice: the exile: the community of returned exiles
decisions.reason: "The exile" here means the people who had been in exile and returned (as in 4:1; 6:19-21; 8:35). The wrong belongs to the community that God had brought back.

decisions.choice: the evening offering: the regular offering made at the temple late in the day
decisions.reason: The law set an offering every morning and every evening (Exodus 29:38-42). The time of the evening offering, in the afternoon, was a time of prayer (1 Kings 18:36; Daniel 9:21). Ezra sat silent from the time he heard the news until then.

decisions.choice: took seriously what God had said (Readable); the returned exiles, the people who came back from exile
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of trembling at God's words. The exile is rendered as the book-wide choices give it.

decisions.choice: "tomaban en serio lo que el Dios de Israel había dicho" (R); "temblaban ante las palabras" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of trembling at God's words (m1), as the English does.

source.text: וּבְמִנְחַ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב קַ֚מְתִּי מִתַּֽעֲנִיתִ֔י וּבְקָרְעִ֥י בִגְדִ֖י וּמְעִילִ֑י וָֽאֶכְרְעָה֙ עַל־בִּרְכַּ֔י וָאֶפְרְשָׂ֥ה כַפַּ֖י אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And at [the] offering of the evening I rose from my humiliation, and in my tearing my garment and my robe, and I bowed on my knees and spread out my palms to YHWH my God.

en.L: And at the evening offering I rose from my humbling, with my garment and my robe torn, and I bowed down on my knees and spread out my palms to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.
en.B: At the evening offering I got up from my fasting, with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees and spread out my hands to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.
en.R: At the time of the evening offering I stopped fasting and got up, still in my torn clothes and coat. I knelt down and held out my hands to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God in prayer.

es.L: Y a la hora de la ofrenda de la tarde me levanté de mi humillación, con mi vestido y mi manto rasgados, y me postré de rodillas y extendí las palmas de mis manos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} mi Dios.
es.B: A la hora de la ofrenda de la tarde me levanté de mi ayuno, con la túnica y el manto rasgados, y caí de rodillas y extendí las manos hacia {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios.
es.R: A la hora de la ofrenda de la tarde dejé el ayuno y me levanté, todavía con mi ropa y mi manto rasgados. Me arrodillé y levanté las manos hacia {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios para orar.

fr.L: Et à l’offrande du soir, je me relevai de mon humiliation, avec mon vêtement et mon manteau déchirés, et je tombai à genoux et j’étendis mes paumes vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu.
fr.B: À l’offrande du soir, je me relevai de mon jeûne, la tunique et le manteau déchirés, je tombai à genoux et je tendis les mains vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu.
fr.R: Au moment de l’offrande du soir, j’ai arrêté de jeûner et je me suis relevé, toujours avec mes vêtements et mon manteau déchirés. Je me suis mis à genoux et j’ai tendu les mains vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu pour prier.

sw.L: Na wakati wa sadaka ya jioni nikainuka kutoka katika kujinyenyekeza kwangu, vazi langu na joho langu yakiwa yameraruka, nikapiga magoti, nikamnyooshea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu viganja vyangu.
sw.B: Wakati wa sadaka ya jioni niliinuka kutoka katika mfungo wangu, kanzu yangu na joho langu vikiwa vimeraruka, nikapiga magoti na kumnyooshea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu mikono yangu.
sw.R: Wakati wa sadaka ya jioni niliacha kufunga, nikainuka, nikiwa bado nimevaa nguo zangu na koti langu vilivyoraruka. Nikapiga magoti, nikamnyooshea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu mikono yangu katika maombi.

vi.L: Và vào lúc dâng tế lễ buổi chiều, tôi đứng dậy khỏi sự hạ mình của tôi, với áo trong và áo choàng đã xé rách, và tôi quỳ gối xuống và giang hai lòng bàn tay ra hướng về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.
vi.B: Đến giờ dâng tế lễ buổi chiều, tôi đứng dậy sau khi kiêng ăn, áo trong và áo choàng vẫn còn rách, rồi tôi quỳ gối xuống và giơ hai tay hướng về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.
vi.R: Đến giờ dâng tế lễ buổi chiều, tôi thôi kiêng ăn và đứng dậy, vẫn mặc áo trong và áo ngoài đã xé rách. Tôi quỳ xuống và giơ hai tay lên cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của tôi.

decisions.choice: my humbling: the self-humbling of fasting and mourning
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to humble or afflict oneself, the phrase the law uses for fasting (Leviticus 16:29, 31). In later Hebrew this noun is the ordinary word for a fast. Ezra had sat through the day without eating, as he does again in 10:6.

decisions.choice: in my tearing my garment and my robe: with the clothes he had already torn
alternatives: and I tore my garment and my robe again
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely describes the state he rose in, still wearing the clothes he had torn in verse 3. It could also mean that he tore them again as he began to pray.

decisions.choice: kneeling and spreading out the palms: the posture of earnest prayer
decisions.reason: Solomon prayed the same way, on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven (1 Kings 8:22, 54). Open, lifted hands show that the one praying is asking and receiving.

decisions.choice: palms (Literal), hands (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the palm or the flat of the hand. Balanced and Readable say hands; Readable adds "in prayer", which the posture means and verse 6 confirms.

decisions.choice: "mfungo wangu" (B); "niliacha kufunga" (R); Literal "kujinyenyekeza kwangu"
decisions.reason: The word is self-humbling, here by fasting, as the English Balanced says.

source.text: וָאֹמְרָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ בֹּ֣שְׁתִּי וְנִכְלַ֔מְתִּי לְהָרִ֧ים אֱלֹהַ֛י פָּנַ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י עֲוֺנֹתֵ֤ינוּ רָבוּ֙ לְמַ֣עְלָה רֹּ֔אשׁ וְאַשְׁמָתֵ֥נוּ גָדְלָ֖ה עַ֥ד לַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, My God, I am ashamed and I am humiliated to lift up, my God, my face to you, for our iniquities have multiplied upward [above our] head, and our guilt has grown great up to the heavens.

en.L: And I said, "My God, I am ashamed and disgraced to lift up my face, my God, to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for our iniquities have multiplied above [our] head, and our guilt has grown great up to the heavens.
en.B: I said, "My God, I am too ashamed and humiliated to lift my face to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God, because our sins are piled higher than our heads, and our guilt reaches up to the heavens.
en.R: I prayed, "My God, I am so ashamed and embarrassed that I cannot look up at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Our sins are so many that they are piled up over our heads. Our guilt is so great that it reaches the sky.

es.L: Y dije: «Dios mío, estoy avergonzado y humillado para levantar mi rostro, Dios mío, hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, porque nuestras iniquidades se han multiplicado por encima de [nuestra] cabeza, y nuestra culpa ha crecido hasta los cielos.
es.B: Dije: «Dios mío, estoy tan avergonzado y humillado que no puedo levantar el rostro hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Dios mío, porque nuestros pecados se han amontonado por encima de nuestra cabeza, y nuestra culpa llega hasta los cielos.
es.R: Oré así: «Dios mío, estoy tan avergonzado y apenado que no puedo levantar los ojos hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Nuestros pecados son tantos que se han amontonado por encima de nuestra cabeza. Nuestra culpa es tan grande que llega hasta el cielo.

fr.L: Et je dis : « Mon Dieu, j’ai honte et je suis confus de lever, mon Dieu, ma face vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, car nos iniquités se sont multipliées par-dessus [notre] tête, et notre culpabilité a grandi jusqu’aux cieux.
fr.B: Je dis : « Mon Dieu, j’ai trop honte et je suis trop humilié pour lever mon visage vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, mon Dieu, car nos péchés se sont amoncelés plus haut que nos têtes, et notre culpabilité s’élève jusqu’aux cieux.
fr.R: J’ai prié : « Mon Dieu, j’ai tellement honte et je suis tellement gêné que je n’ose pas lever les yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Nos péchés sont si nombreux qu’ils s’entassent par-dessus nos têtes. Notre culpabilité est si grande qu’elle monte jusqu’au ciel.

sw.L: Nami nikasema, "Ee Mungu wangu, ninaona aibu na kufedheheka kuinua uso wangu, Ee Mungu wangu, kwako {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, kwa maana maovu yetu yameongezeka juu ya kichwa [chetu], na hatia yetu imekua mpaka mbinguni.
sw.B: Nikasema, "Ee Mungu wangu, ninaona aibu sana na kufedheheka kuinua uso wangu kwako {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Mungu wangu, kwa sababu dhambi zetu zimerundikana juu kuliko vichwa vyetu, na hatia yetu imefika mpaka mbinguni.
sw.R: Niliomba, "Mungu wangu, ninaona aibu na kufedheheka sana hata siwezi kukutazama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}. Dhambi zetu ni nyingi mno, zimerundikana juu ya vichwa vyetu. Hatia yetu ni kubwa sana hata imefika angani.

vi.L: Và tôi nói: "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, con hổ thẹn và xấu hổ không dám ngước mặt lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, vì tội ác của chúng con đã chồng chất cao hơn đầu [chúng con], và tội lỗi của chúng con đã lớn đến tận các tầng trời.
vi.B: Tôi thưa: "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, con hổ thẹn và nhục nhã quá, không dám ngước mặt lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, vì tội lỗi của chúng con đã chồng chất cao hơn đầu chúng con, và sự phạm tội của chúng con đã lên đến tận trời.
vi.R: Tôi cầu nguyện: "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, con xấu hổ và nhục nhã đến nỗi không dám ngước nhìn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Tội lỗi của chúng con nhiều đến nỗi đã chất cao hơn đầu chúng con. Sự phạm tội của chúng con lớn đến nỗi đã lên tới trời.

decisions.choice: ashamed and humiliated: two words for deep disgrace
decisions.reason: The two verbs are often paired for the shame of someone who has been exposed as guilty (Jeremiah 31:19). Together they say that Ezra cannot even face God.

decisions.choice: above our head ... to the heavens: sins like rising water that covers a person, and like a heap reaching the sky
decisions.reason: "My iniquities have gone over my head" is the picture of a man drowning (Psalm 38:5). The second picture is of guilt piled so high it reaches heaven. Both say the guilt is beyond what the people can deal with.

decisions.choice: our iniquities, our guilt: Ezra counts himself among the guilty
decisions.reason: Ezra is not said to have married a foreign wife, yet from here on he says "we" and "our", confessing the sin of his people as his own, as Nehemiah (Nehemiah 1:6) and Daniel (Daniel 9:5) do in their prayers.

decisions.choice: iniquities (Literal), sins (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means a wrong and the guilt it brings. Literal keeps the traditional "iniquities"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

decisions.choice: God addressed as "tú" with deity_pronoun; "iniquidades" (L), "pecados" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Ezra's prayer (verses 6-15) speaks to God as "tú", and God's free pronouns take the setting where the English has one; Literal keeps the traditional "iniquidades", Balanced and Readable the everyday word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: God is addressed with "wewe", and the free forms ("wewe", "yako", "kwako") carry the deity span through the prayer
decisions.reason: As the Swahili style guide: the "u-" and "-ku-" inside verbs cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives carry the setting, and a pronoun at the start of a sentence is plain.

decisions.choice: "maovu" (L), "dhambi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional word for iniquity; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as the English.

decisions.choice: the prayer in the tenses of speech; God addressed as "tu"
decisions.reason: Ezra's prayer (9:6-15) is speech, so its history is told in the present and the passé composé at every level, as the terms note sets; God is "tu", with the deity pronoun setting on every free pronoun.

decisions.choice: con, chúng con; Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con; Ngài
decisions.reason: In his prayer Ezra speaks to God as "con" and "chúng con", saying "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con", and calls God "Ngài", as the terms note sets for Ezra 9:6-15; the narration around the prayer keeps "tôi".

decisions.choice: tội ác (Literal); tội lỗi (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity keeps the stronger "tội ác" at Literal, as the English keeps "iniquities"; Balanced and Readable say "tội lỗi", and "sự phạm tội" for guilt.

source.text: מִימֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ בְּאַשְׁמָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּבַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֡ינוּ נִתַּ֡נּוּ אֲנַחְנוּ֩ מְלָכֵ֨ינוּ כֹהֲנֵ֜ינוּ בְּיַ֣ד׀מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֲרָצ֗וֹת בַּחֶ֜רֶב בַּשְּׁבִ֧י וּבַבִּזָּ֛ה וּבְבֹ֥שֶׁת פָּנִ֖ים כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] days of our fathers we [have been] in great guilt until this day; and in our iniquities we have been given, we, our kings, our priests, into [the] hand of [the] kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to plunder, and to shame of face, as this day.

en.L: From the days of our fathers until this day we [have been] in great guilt, and because of our iniquities we, our kings, [and] our priests have been given into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame of face, as [it is] this day.
en.B: Ever since the days of our ancestors we have been deeply guilty, down to this very day. Because of our sins, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to open shame, as we are today.
en.R: From the time of our ancestors until now, we have been very guilty. Because of our sins, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} handed us over to the kings of other lands, together with our kings and our priests. They killed us with swords, took us away as prisoners, robbed us, and put us to shame. And that is how it is today.

es.L: Desde los días de nuestros padres hasta este día [hemos estado] en gran culpa, y por nuestras iniquidades nosotros, nuestros reyes [y] nuestros sacerdotes hemos sido entregados en mano de los reyes de las tierras, a la espada, al cautiverio, al saqueo y a la vergüenza del rostro, como [sucede] este día.
es.B: Desde los días de nuestros antepasados hemos sido muy culpables, hasta el día de hoy. Por nuestros pecados, nosotros, nuestros reyes y nuestros sacerdotes hemos sido entregados a los reyes de las tierras, a la espada, al cautiverio, al saqueo y a la vergüenza pública, como estamos hoy.
es.R: Desde el tiempo de nuestros antepasados hasta ahora, hemos sido muy culpables. Por nuestros pecados, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} nos entregaste a los reyes de otras tierras, junto con nuestros reyes y nuestros sacerdotes. Nos mataron a espada, nos llevaron prisioneros, nos robaron y nos avergonzaron. Y así estamos hoy.

fr.L: Depuis les jours de nos pères jusqu’à ce jour, nous [sommes] dans une grande culpabilité, et à cause de nos iniquités, nous, nos rois [et] nos prêtres, nous avons été livrés entre les mains des rois des pays, à l’épée, à la captivité, au pillage et à la honte du visage, comme [c’est le cas] aujourd’hui.
fr.B: Depuis le temps de nos ancêtres jusqu’à ce jour, nous sommes gravement coupables. À cause de nos péchés, nous, nos rois et nos prêtres, nous avons été livrés aux rois des pays, à l’épée, à la captivité, au pillage et à la honte publique, comme nous le sommes aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Depuis le temps de nos ancêtres jusqu’à maintenant, nous sommes très coupables. À cause de nos péchés, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as livrés aux rois des autres pays, avec nos rois et nos prêtres. Ils nous ont tués par l’épée, emmenés comme prisonniers, pillés et couverts de honte. Et c’est encore comme cela aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Tangu siku za baba zetu mpaka siku hii ya leo tumekuwa katika hatia kubwa, na kwa sababu ya maovu yetu sisi, wafalme wetu, [na] makuhani wetu tumetiwa mkononi mwa wafalme wa nchi, kwa upanga, kwa utumwa, kwa kutekwa nyara, na kwa aibu ya uso, kama [ilivyo] siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Tangu siku za wazee wetu tumekuwa na hatia kubwa, mpaka leo hii. Kwa sababu ya dhambi zetu, sisi, wafalme wetu na makuhani wetu tumetiwa mikononi mwa wafalme wa nchi, kwa upanga, kwa kuchukuliwa mateka, kwa kunyang'anywa mali na kwa aibu ya wazi, kama tulivyo leo.
sw.R: Tangu wakati wa wazee wetu mpaka sasa, tumekuwa na hatia kubwa. Kwa sababu ya dhambi zetu, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulitutia mikononi mwa wafalme wa nchi nyingine, pamoja na wafalme wetu na makuhani wetu. Walituua kwa upanga, wakatuchukua mateka, wakatunyang'anya mali, wakatuaibisha. Na ndivyo ilivyo hata leo.

vi.L: Từ những ngày của tổ phụ chúng con cho đến ngày nay, chúng con [đã ở] trong tội lỗi lớn, và vì tội ác của chúng con, chúng con, các vua chúng con [và] các thầy tế lễ chúng con đã bị phó vào tay các vua của các xứ, cho gươm, cho cảnh phu tù, cho sự cướp bóc và cho sự hổ mặt, như [đang có] ngày nay.
vi.B: Từ thời tổ tiên chúng con cho đến ngày nay, chúng con đã phạm tội nặng nề. Vì tội lỗi của chúng con, chúng con, các vua và các thầy tế lễ của chúng con đã bị phó vào tay các vua của các xứ, bị gươm giết, bị bắt làm phu tù, bị cướp bóc và bị sỉ nhục công khai, như chúng con đang chịu ngày nay.
vi.R: Từ thời tổ tiên chúng con cho đến nay, chúng con đã phạm tội rất nặng. Vì tội lỗi của chúng con, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phó chúng con cùng các vua và các thầy tế lễ của chúng con vào tay các vua của những nước khác. Họ đã dùng gươm giết chúng con, bắt chúng con đi làm tù binh, cướp bóc chúng con và làm cho chúng con bị sỉ nhục. Ngày nay vẫn còn như vậy.

decisions.choice: we have been given into the hand of the kings of the lands: God handed his people over to foreign kings
decisions.reason: The passive does not name who gave them over, but the prayer means God, as Nehemiah 9:27, 30 says outright. The kings of the lands are the kings of Assyria, Babylon and Persia who ruled Israel from the fall of the kingdoms until Ezra's day (Nehemiah 9:32).

decisions.choice: shame of face: public disgrace
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures shame that shows on the face. Daniel uses the same words in his confession: "to us shame of face, as at this day" (Daniel 9:7).

decisions.choice: as this day: as it still is now
decisions.reason: The punishment is not only in the past. The people are still subjects of foreign kings (9:9; Nehemiah 9:36-37).

decisions.choice: you handed us over (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who handed them over, which the passive implies (Nehemiah 9:30). Literal and Balanced keep the passive.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה כִּמְעַט־רֶגַע֩ הָיְתָ֨ה תְחִנָּ֜ה מֵאֵ֣ת׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לְהַשְׁאִ֥יר לָ֨נוּ֙ פְּלֵיטָ֔ה וְלָתֶת־לָ֥נוּ יָתֵ֖ד בִּמְק֣וֹם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ לְהָאִ֤יר עֵינֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וּלְתִתֵּ֛נוּ מִֽחְיָ֥ה מְעַ֖ט בְּעַבְדֻתֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, like a little moment, has been favor from YHWH our God, to leave to us an escaped remnant and to give to us a tent peg in [the] place of his holiness, to make shine our eyes, our God, and to give us a little reviving in our slavery.

en.L: And now, for a little moment, favor has come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to leave us an escaped remnant and to give us a tent peg in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place, that our God may brighten our eyes and give us a little reviving in our slavery.
en.B: But now, for a short time, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has shown us favor. He has left us a remnant who escaped and has given us a secure hold in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place. So our God has brightened our eyes and given us a little new life in our slavery.
en.R: But now, for a short time, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has been kind to us. He has let some of us survive and come back. He has given us a firm hold in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place, like a tent peg driven into the ground. Our God has given us new hope and a little new life while we are still slaves.

es.L: Y ahora, por un breve momento, ha habido favor de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, para dejarnos un remanente que escapó y para darnos una estaca en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo, para que nuestro Dios ilumine nuestros ojos y nos dé un poco de vida en nuestra esclavitud.
es.B: Pero ahora, por un poco de tiempo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios nos ha mostrado favor. Nos ha dejado un remanente que escapó y nos ha dado un lugar seguro en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo. Así nuestro Dios ha iluminado nuestros ojos y nos ha dado un poco de nueva vida en nuestra esclavitud.
es.R: Pero ahora, por un poco de tiempo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios ha sido bondadoso con nosotros. Ha dejado que algunos de nosotros sobrevivamos y regresemos. Nos ha dado un lugar firme en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar santo, como una estaca clavada en la tierra. Nuestro Dios nos ha dado nueva esperanza y un poco de nueva vida mientras todavía somos esclavos.

fr.L: Et maintenant, pour un court instant, une faveur est venue {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu, pour nous laisser un reste de rescapés et nous donner un piquet dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint, afin que notre Dieu éclaire nos yeux et nous donne un peu de vie dans notre esclavage.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, pour un peu de temps, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu nous a fait grâce. Il nous a laissé un reste de rescapés et nous a donné un appui solide dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint. Ainsi notre Dieu a fait briller nos yeux et nous a rendu un peu de vie dans notre esclavage.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, pour un peu de temps, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu a été bon pour nous. Il a laissé quelques-uns d’entre nous survivre et revenir. Il nous a donné une place solide dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} lieu saint, comme un piquet de tente bien planté dans le sol. Notre Dieu nous a donné un nouvel espoir et un peu de vie nouvelle, alors que nous sommes encore esclaves.

sw.L: Na sasa, kwa kitambo kidogo, kibali kimetoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, kutuachia mabaki yaliyookoka na kutupa kigingi katika mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu, ili Mungu wetu ayatie nuru macho yetu na kutupa uhai mpya kidogo katika utumwa wetu.
sw.B: Lakini sasa, kwa muda mfupi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu ametuonyesha kibali. Ametuachia mabaki yaliyookoka na ametupa mahali imara pa kushikilia katika mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu. Hivyo Mungu wetu ameyatia nuru macho yetu na kutupa uhai mpya kidogo katika utumwa wetu.
sw.R: Lakini sasa, kwa muda mfupi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu ametuonyesha wema. Amewaacha baadhi yetu waokoke na kurudi. Ametupa mahali imara pa kushikilia katika mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} patakatifu, kama kigingi cha hema kilichopigiliwa ardhini. Mungu wetu ametupa tumaini jipya na uhai mpya kidogo wakati bado tu watumwa.

vi.L: Và bây giờ, trong một chốc lát, ân huệ đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chúng con, để chừa lại cho chúng con một số người thoát nạn và ban cho chúng con một cây cọc lều trong nơi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để Đức Chúa Trời chúng con làm sáng mắt chúng con và ban cho chúng con một chút hồi sinh trong cảnh nô lệ của chúng con.
vi.B: Nhưng bây giờ, trong một thời gian ngắn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chúng con đã ban ơn cho chúng con. Ngài đã chừa lại cho chúng con một số người thoát nạn và ban cho chúng con một chỗ đứng vững vàng trong nơi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Như vậy Đức Chúa Trời chúng con đã làm cho mắt chúng con sáng lên và ban cho chúng con một chút sức sống mới trong cảnh nô lệ.
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ, trong một thời gian ngắn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chúng con đã tỏ lòng nhân từ với chúng con. Ngài đã để cho một số chúng con sống sót và trở về. Ngài đã ban cho chúng con một chỗ đứng vững chắc trong nơi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, như cây cọc lều đóng chặt xuống đất. Đức Chúa Trời chúng con đã ban cho chúng con niềm hy vọng mới và một chút sức sống mới, dù chúng con vẫn còn làm nô lệ.

decisions.choice: for a little moment: a brief time
decisions.reason: The time of favor is short set against the long history of guilt in verse 7, which runs from the days of the ancestors. It may also hint that the favor could quickly be lost (verse 14).

decisions.choice: an escaped remnant: those who survived the disaster
decisions.reason: The word means those who escaped. It is the key word of the prayer (verses 8, 13, 14, 15): the returned community is what is left of Israel, and Ezra fears it may be lost.

decisions.choice: a tent peg in his holy place: a secure foothold in Jerusalem, where the temple stands
alternatives: a nail in his holy place
decisions.reason: A tent peg is driven firmly into the ground and holds the tent. Isaiah uses the picture of a peg fastened in a sure place (Isaiah 22:23) and of Jerusalem as a tent whose pegs are never pulled up (Isaiah 33:20). The holy place may be the temple itself or Jerusalem as the place of God's temple.

decisions.choice: to brighten our eyes: to give new strength and hope
decisions.reason: Eyes that brighten are a picture of renewed life and strength (1 Samuel 14:27, 29; Psalm 13:4).

decisions.choice: a tent peg (Literal), a secure hold (Balanced), a firm hold ... like a tent peg (Readable); a little new life
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture. Balanced says what it means; Readable says what it means and keeps the picture as a comparison. "Reviving" becomes "new life".

decisions.choice: "un remanente que escapó"; "una estaca" (L); "un lugar seguro" (B); "un lugar firme ... como una estaca" (R)
decisions.reason: "Remanente" for the survivors, as the terms note sets it; Literal keeps the tent peg, Balanced says what it means, Readable keeps it as a comparison, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "kigingi" (L), "mahali imara pa kushikilia" (B), "... kama kigingi cha hema" (R); "mabaki yaliyookoka" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the tent peg, Balanced says what it means, Readable keeps the picture as a comparison; "mabaki" is the terms-note word for the remnant.

decisions.choice: "un reste de rescapés" (Literal, Balanced); "quelques-uns d'entre nous survivre" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The key word of the prayer (verses 8, 13, 14, 15), worded with "reste", the French term for the remnant (2 Kings 19:31), and "rescapés" for those who escaped.

decisions.choice: một cây cọc lều (Literal); một chỗ đứng vững vàng (Balanced); một chỗ đứng vững chắc ... như cây cọc lều (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the tent peg, with the word of Judges 4:21; Balanced says what it means, and Readable says what it means and keeps the picture as a comparison (m3).

decisions.choice: một số người thoát nạn (Literal, Balanced); một số chúng con sống sót (Readable)
decisions.reason: The escaped remnant is the key word of the prayer (verses 8, 13, 14, 15); "thoát nạn" keeps the sense of escaping a disaster at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: כִּֽי־עֲבָדִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וּבְעַבְדֻ֔תֵנוּלֹ֥א עֲזָבָ֖נוּ אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיַּט־עָלֵ֣ינוּ חֶ֡סֶד לִפְנֵי֩ מַלְכֵ֨י פָרַ֜ס לָֽתֶת־לָ֣נוּ מִֽחְיָ֗ה לְרוֹמֵ֞ם אֶת־בֵּ֤ית אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּלְהַעֲמִ֣יד אֶת־חָרְבֹתָ֔יו וְלָֽתֶת־לָ֣נוּ גָדֵ֔ר בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For slaves [are] we, and in our slavery not has forsaken us our God, and he has extended to us steadfast love before [the] kings of Persia, to give to us reviving, to raise up the house of our God and to set up its ruins, and to give to us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.

en.L: For we [are] slaves, yet in our slavery our God has not forsaken us, but has extended to us steadfast love before the kings of Persia, to give us reviving, to raise up the house of our God and to restore its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
en.B: We are slaves, but our God has not abandoned us in our slavery. He has shown us faithful love in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and restore its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: We are slaves, but our God has not left us alone in our slavery. He has shown us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and made the kings of Persia kind to us. He has given us new life, so that we could rebuild the temple of our God and repair its ruins. He has given us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.

es.L: Porque esclavos [somos], pero en nuestra esclavitud nuestro Dios no nos ha abandonado, sino que ha extendido hacia nosotros amor leal delante de los reyes de Persia, para darnos vida, para levantar la casa de nuestro Dios y restaurar sus ruinas, y para darnos un muro en Judá y en Jerusalén.
es.B: Somos esclavos, pero nuestro Dios no nos ha abandonado en nuestra esclavitud. Nos ha mostrado amor fiel delante de los reyes de Persia, dándonos nueva vida para reedificar la casa de nuestro Dios y restaurar sus ruinas, y dándonos un muro de protección en Judá y en Jerusalén.
es.R: Somos esclavos, pero nuestro Dios no nos ha dejado solos en nuestra esclavitud. Nos ha mostrado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor fiel y ha hecho que los reyes de Persia sean bondadosos con nosotros. Nos ha dado nueva vida, para que pudiéramos reconstruir el templo de nuestro Dios y reparar sus ruinas. Nos ha dado un muro de protección en Judá y en Jerusalén.

fr.L: Car nous [sommes] esclaves, mais dans notre esclavage notre Dieu ne nous a pas abandonnés ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a étendu sur nous {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour loyal devant les rois de Perse, pour nous rendre la vie, pour relever la maison de notre Dieu et en restaurer les ruines, et pour nous donner un mur en Juda et à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Nous sommes esclaves, mais notre Dieu ne nous a pas abandonnés dans notre esclavage. Il nous a montré {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour fidèle devant les rois de Perse : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a rendu la vie pour rebâtir la maison de notre Dieu et en restaurer les ruines, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné un mur de protection en Juda et à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Nous sommes esclaves, mais notre Dieu ne nous a pas laissés seuls dans notre esclavage. Il nous a montré {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour fidèle et il a rendu les rois de Perse bienveillants envers nous. Il nous a rendu la vie pour que nous puissions reconstruire le temple de notre Dieu et réparer ses ruines. Il nous a donné un mur de protection en Juda et à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Kwa maana sisi [ni] watumwa, lakini katika utumwa wetu Mungu wetu hakutuacha, bali ametunyooshea upendo usiokoma mbele ya wafalme wa Uajemi, kutupa uhai mpya, kuisimamisha nyumba ya Mungu wetu na kuyatengeneza magofu yake, na kutupa ukuta katika Yuda na katika Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Sisi ni watumwa, lakini Mungu wetu hakutuacha katika utumwa wetu. Ametuonyesha upendo usiokoma mbele ya wafalme wa Uajemi, akatupa uhai mpya ili tuijenge upya nyumba ya Mungu wetu na kuyatengeneza magofu yake, akatupa ukuta wa ulinzi katika Yuda na Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Sisi ni watumwa, lakini Mungu wetu hakutuacha peke yetu katika utumwa wetu. Ametuonyesha upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usiokoma, akawafanya wafalme wa Uajemi watutendee mema. Ametupa uhai mpya, ili tulijenge upya hekalu la Mungu wetu na kuyatengeneza magofu yake. Ametupa ukuta wa ulinzi katika Yuda na Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Vì chúng con [là] nô lệ, nhưng trong cảnh nô lệ của chúng con, Đức Chúa Trời chúng con không lìa bỏ chúng con, mà đã tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín cho chúng con trước mặt các vua Ba Tư, để ban cho chúng con sự hồi sinh, để dựng lại nhà của Đức Chúa Trời chúng con và sửa lại những nơi đổ nát của nó, và để ban cho chúng con một bức tường tại Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Chúng con là nô lệ, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời chúng con không bỏ rơi chúng con trong cảnh nô lệ. Ngài đã tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín cho chúng con trước mặt các vua Ba Tư, ban cho chúng con sức sống mới để xây lại nhà của Đức Chúa Trời chúng con và sửa sang những nơi đổ nát, và ban cho chúng con một bức tường che chở tại Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Chúng con là nô lệ, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời chúng con không bỏ mặc chúng con trong cảnh nô lệ. Ngài đã tỏ tình thương không hề thay đổi của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho chúng con và khiến các vua Ba Tư đối xử tốt với chúng con. Ngài đã ban cho chúng con sức sống mới, để chúng con có thể xây lại đền thờ của Đức Chúa Trời chúng con và sửa sang những nơi đổ nát. Ngài đã ban cho chúng con một bức tường che chở tại Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem.

decisions.choice: we are slaves ... before the kings of Persia: subjects of the Persian empire
decisions.reason: The returned exiles were not free; they lived as subjects of Persia and paid its taxes (4:13; Nehemiah 9:36-37). Yet the Persian kings had let them return and rebuild: Cyrus (1:1-4), Darius (6:1-12) and Artaxerxes (7:11-26).

decisions.choice: he has extended steadfast love before the kings: God has shown his covenant loyalty by giving them favor with the kings
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 7:28: God "extended steadfast love to me before the king". The word for steadfast love is God's faithful, committed love to his people. Here it works through the decisions of foreign kings.

decisions.choice: a wall in Judah and Jerusalem: protection, not yet the city wall
alternatives: a city wall in Judah and Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word is not the usual word for a city wall but for a stone wall or fence, such as the wall around a vineyard (Isaiah 5:5; Psalm 80:13). A wall around the whole of Judah cannot be a building, so it is a picture of the security God gave under Persian rule. Jerusalem's walls were rebuilt later, under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 2-6).

decisions.choice: slaves, slavery at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "slave" where slavery itself is the point. Ezra speaks of the people's subjection to foreign kings, set against the freedom they had lost (Nehemiah 9:36-37), so "servants" would weaken what he says.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal), faithful love (Balanced, Readable); the house of our God, the temple of our God (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the terms used across the Old Testament books. Readable adds that God made the kings kind to them, which is what showing love "before" the kings means here (7:27-28).

decisions.choice: "esclavos", "esclavitud" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: slavery itself is the point here, the people's subjection to foreign kings, so "esclavo" stands at every level, not "siervo".

decisions.choice: "watumwa", "utumwa" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: the people's subjection to foreign kings is the point, so the word for slavery is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: deity pronoun spans on "il" and "son" at every level
decisions.reason: French needs a free pronoun for God where the English Literal and Balanced have none ("il a étendu", "son amour"), so the setting goes on it at every level.

decisions.choice: nô lệ, cảnh nô lệ (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the point is the people's subjection to foreign kings (m1), slavery itself, so "nô lệ" is used at every level, as the terms note allows for slavery; God's servants elsewhere stay "đầy tớ".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֛ה מַה־נֹּאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֑את כִּ֥י עָזַ֖בְנוּ מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now what shall we say, our God, after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,

en.L: And now, our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments,
en.B: And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments,
en.R: Now, our God, what can we say after all this? We have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

es.L: Y ahora, Dios nuestro, ¿qué diremos después de esto? Porque hemos abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} mandamientos,
es.B: Y ahora, Dios nuestro, ¿qué podemos decir después de esto? Porque hemos abandonado {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} mandamientos,
es.R: Ahora, Dios nuestro, ¿qué podemos decir después de todo esto? Nos hemos apartado de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} mandamientos.

fr.L: Et maintenant, notre Dieu, que dirons-nous après cela ? Car nous avons abandonné {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} commandements,
fr.B: Et maintenant, notre Dieu, que pouvons-nous dire après cela ? Car nous avons abandonné {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} commandements,
fr.R: Maintenant, notre Dieu, que pouvons-nous dire après tout cela ? Nous nous sommes détournés de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} commandements.

sw.L: Na sasa, Ee Mungu wetu, tuseme nini baada ya haya? Kwa maana tumeziacha amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}},
sw.B: Na sasa, Ee Mungu wetu, tuseme nini baada ya haya? Kwa maana tumeziacha amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}},
sw.R: Sasa, Mungu wetu, tuseme nini baada ya hayo yote? Tumeziacha amri {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}.

vi.L: Và bây giờ, lạy Đức Chúa Trời chúng con, sau điều này chúng con sẽ nói gì? Vì chúng con đã lìa bỏ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},
vi.B: Và bây giờ, lạy Đức Chúa Trời chúng con, sau mọi điều ấy chúng con còn biết nói gì? Vì chúng con đã lìa bỏ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},
vi.R: Lạy Đức Chúa Trời chúng con, sau mọi điều ấy, chúng con còn biết nói gì nữa? Chúng con đã quay lưng với các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: after this: after all God's kindness just described
decisions.reason: "This" most naturally points back to verses 8-9: after God has shown such favor, the people have answered by breaking his commands. The question has no answer; there is nothing they can say in their defense.

decisions.choice: we have forsaken your commandments: we have abandoned what you commanded
decisions.reason: To forsake God's commandments is to leave them behind deliberately (1 Kings 18:18). The commandment in question is quoted in verses 11-12.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתָ בְּיַ֨ד עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֤ם בָּאִים֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ אֶ֤רֶץ נִדָּה֙ הִ֔יא בְּנִדַּ֖ת עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת בְּתוֹעֲבֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִלְא֛וּהָ מִפֶּ֥ה אֶל־פֶּ֖ה בְּטֻמְאָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: which you commanded by [the] hand of your slaves the prophets, saying, The land which you [are] going [to] to possess it, a land of impurity it [is], by [the] impurity of [the] peoples of the lands, by their abominations, which they have filled it from mouth to mouth with their uncleanness.

en.L: which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves the prophets, saying, 'The land that you are entering to possess is a land of impurity, through the impurity of the peoples of the lands, through their abominations, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth with their uncleanness.
en.B: which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said, 'The land you are entering to take possession of is a land made impure by the impurity of the peoples of the lands, by their detestable practices. They have filled it from one end to the other with their uncleanness.
en.R: You gave those commands through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets. You said, 'The land you are going into to take as your own is unclean. The peoples living in the land have made it unclean by the disgusting things they do. They have filled it with their filth from one end to the other.

es.L: que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} mandaste por medio de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} esclavos los profetas, diciendo: “La tierra en la que {{plural_you:entran|entráis}} para poseerla es una tierra de impureza, por la impureza de los pueblos de las tierras, por sus abominaciones, con las que la han llenado de un extremo a otro con su inmundicia.
es.B: que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} diste por medio de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos los profetas cuando dijiste: “La tierra en la que {{plural_you:entran|entráis}} para tomar posesión de ella es una tierra contaminada por la impureza de los pueblos de las tierras, por sus prácticas detestables. La han llenado de un extremo a otro con su inmundicia.
es.R: Tú diste esos mandamientos por medio de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos los profetas. Dijiste: “La tierra en la que {{plural_you:van a entrar|vais a entrar}} para hacerla suya está impura. Los pueblos que viven allí la han hecho impura con las cosas repugnantes que hacen. La han llenado de su suciedad de un extremo a otro.

fr.L: que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as prescrits par la main de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} esclaves les prophètes, en disant : “Le pays dans lequel vous entrez pour le posséder est un pays d’impureté, par l’impureté des peuples des pays, par leurs abominations, dont ils l’ont rempli d’un bout à l’autre avec leur souillure.
fr.B: que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as donnés par {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs les prophètes, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit : “Le pays où vous entrez pour en prendre possession est un pays rendu impur par l’impureté des peuples des pays, par leurs pratiques abominables. Ils l’ont rempli de leur souillure d’un bout à l’autre.
fr.R: Tu as donné ces commandements par {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs les prophètes. Tu as dit : “Le pays où vous allez entrer pour le prendre est impur. Les peuples qui y habitent l’ont rendu impur par les choses horribles qu’ils font. Ils l’ont rempli de leurs saletés d’un bout à l’autre.

sw.L: ulizoziamuru kwa mkono wa watumwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} manabii, ukisema, 'Nchi mnayoingia kuimiliki ni nchi ya unajisi, kwa unajisi wa mataifa ya nchi, kwa machukizo yao, ambayo kwayo wameijaza kutoka mdomo hadi mdomo kwa uchafu wao.
sw.B: ulizozitoa kupitia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} manabii, uliposema, 'Nchi mnayoiingia kuimiliki ni nchi iliyotiwa unajisi kwa unajisi wa mataifa ya nchi, kwa desturi zao za kuchukiza. Wameijaza kwa uchafu wao kutoka mwisho mmoja hadi mwingine.
sw.R: Ulitoa amri hizo kupitia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} manabii. Ulisema, 'Nchi mnayoiingia kuifanya yenu ni najisi. Watu walioishi katika nchi wameitia unajisi kwa mambo ya kuchukiza wanayoyafanya. Wameijaza kwa uchafu wao kutoka mwisho mmoja hadi mwingine.

vi.L: là những điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền bởi tay các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri, rằng: 'Đất mà các ngươi đang vào để chiếm hữu là một đất ô uế, bởi sự ô uế của các dân của các xứ, bởi những điều ghê tởm của họ, mà họ đã làm cho đầy đất từ đầu này đến đầu kia bằng sự dơ bẩn của họ.
vi.B: là những điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban qua các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: 'Đất mà các ngươi sắp vào để chiếm hữu là một đất bị ô uế bởi sự ô uế của các dân của các xứ, bởi những thói tục ghê tởm của họ. Họ đã làm cho đất đầy dẫy sự dơ bẩn của họ từ đầu này đến đầu kia.
vi.R: Ngài đã ban các điều răn ấy qua các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là các nhà tiên tri. Ngài phán: 'Đất mà các ngươi sắp vào để nhận làm sản nghiệp là đất ô uế. Các dân sống trong xứ đã làm cho đất ra ô uế bởi những điều gớm ghiếc họ làm. Họ đã làm cho đất đầy dẫy sự dơ bẩn của họ từ đầu này đến đầu kia.

decisions.choice: the prophets' words: a summary of the law's warnings, not a quotation of one passage
decisions.reason: No single passage says these exact words. The prayer gathers what the law says about the land and its peoples (Leviticus 18:24-30; Deuteronomy 7:1-6; 23:7) and joins it with what the prophets later said. Moses himself is counted among the prophets (Deuteronomy 18:15; Hosea 12:14).

decisions.choice: impurity, uncleanness: defilement that makes the land unfit for God's people
decisions.reason: The first word is the one the law uses for a woman's monthly impurity; the prophets use it for the moral and religious defilement of the land (Ezekiel 36:17). The law says the nations defiled the land by their practices so that it "vomited" them out (Leviticus 18:25-28).

decisions.choice: from mouth to mouth: from one end to the other
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures something filled up to the brim, from one opening to the other (2 Kings 10:21; 21:16).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal), servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophets are God's servants; this follows the style guide's rule for the word, since slavery itself is not the point here.

decisions.choice: "esclavos" (L), "siervos" (B, R); plural_you inside the quoted command
decisions.reason: The prophets are God's servants, so the usual rule holds ("esclavo" at Literal only), as the English does; the command quoted in verses 11-12 is to Israel as a people, so its "you" is the plural setting.

decisions.choice: "d'un bout à l'autre"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom "from mouth to mouth" has no sense in French; Literal gives its meaning, as Balanced and Readable do.

decisions.choice: các đầy tớ của Ngài là các nhà tiên tri
decisions.reason: God's servants the prophets are "đầy tớ" at every level, Literal included, as the terms note sets; the English Literal has "slaves". God speaks to the people as "các ngươi".

source.text: וְ֠עַתָּה בְּֽנוֹתֵיכֶ֞ם אַל־תִּתְּנ֣וּ לִבְנֵיהֶ֗ם וּבְנֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אַל־תִּשְׂא֣וּ לִבְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־תִדְרְשׁ֧וּ שְׁלֹמָ֛ם וְטוֹבָתָ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן תֶּחֶזְק֗וּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּם֙ אֶת־ט֣וּב הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now your daughters do not give to their sons, and their daughters do not take for your sons, and do not seek their peace and their good until forever, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and cause [it] to be inherited by your sons until forever.

en.L: And now, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons, and do not seek their peace or their good forever, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave [it] as an inheritance to your sons forever.'
en.B: So do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong, eat the good things of the land, and leave it to your {{gender:children|sons}} as an inheritance forever.'
en.R: So do not let your daughters marry their sons, and do not let your sons marry their daughters. Never try to make peace with them or help them do well. Then you will be strong. You will enjoy the good things the land produces, and you will leave it to your {{gender:children|sons}} to own forever.'

es.L: Ahora, pues, no {{plural_you:den|deis}} {{plural_you:sus hijas|vuestras hijas}} a sus hijos, ni {{plural_you:tomen|toméis}} sus hijas para {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}, ni {{plural_you:busquen|busquéis}} nunca su paz ni su bien, para que {{plural_you:sean fuertes y coman|seáis fuertes y comáis}} el bien de la tierra y la {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} en herencia a {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} para siempre”.
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:den|deis}} {{plural_you:sus hijas|vuestras hijas}} en matrimonio a los hijos de ellos, ni {{plural_you:tomen|toméis}} a sus hijas para {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}, y nunca {{plural_you:procuren|procuréis}} su paz ni su prosperidad, para que {{plural_you:sean fuertes, coman|seáis fuertes, comáis}} los bienes de la tierra y la {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} en herencia a {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} para siempre”.
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:sus hijas|vuestras hijas}} se casen con los hijos de ellos, ni que {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} se casen con las hijas de ellos. Nunca {{plural_you:traten|tratéis}} de hacer la paz con ellos ni de ayudarlos a prosperar. Así {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} fuertes. {{plural_you:Disfrutarán|Disfrutaréis}} de las cosas buenas que produce la tierra, y se la {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} a {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}} para que sea suya para siempre”.

fr.L: Et maintenant, ne donnez pas vos filles à leurs fils, et ne prenez pas leurs filles pour vos fils, et ne recherchez jamais leur paix ni leur bien, afin que vous soyez forts, que vous mangiez les bons produits du pays et que vous [le] laissiez en héritage à vos fils pour toujours.”
fr.B: Ne donnez donc pas vos filles en mariage à leurs fils, ne prenez pas leurs filles pour vos fils, et ne recherchez jamais leur paix ni leur prospérité, afin que vous soyez forts, que vous mangiez les bonnes choses du pays et que vous le laissiez pour toujours en héritage à vos {{gender:enfants|fils}}.”
fr.R: Ne laissez donc pas vos filles épouser leurs fils, et ne laissez pas vos fils épouser leurs filles. N’essayez jamais de faire la paix avec eux ni de les aider à prospérer. Alors vous serez forts. Vous profiterez des bonnes choses que produit le pays, et vous le laisserez pour toujours à vos {{gender:enfants|fils}}.”

sw.L: Basi sasa, msiwape wana wao binti zenu, wala msiwatwalie wana wenu binti zao, wala msiitafute amani yao wala mema yao milele, ili mpate kuwa na nguvu na kula mema ya nchi na kuwaachia wana wenu [iwe] urithi milele.'
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwaoze binti zenu kwa wana wao, wala msiwaoe binti zao kwa ajili ya wana wenu, wala msiitafute kamwe amani yao wala kufanikiwa kwao, ili mpate kuwa na nguvu, mle mema ya nchi, na kuwaachia watoto wenu kuwa urithi milele.'
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiwaache binti zenu waolewe na wana wao, wala msiwaache wana wenu waoe binti zao. Kamwe msijaribu kufanya amani nao wala kuwasaidia wafanikiwe. Ndipo mtakapokuwa na nguvu. Mtafurahia mema ambayo nchi inazaa, na mtawaachia watoto wenu iwe mali yao milele.'

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, đừng gả con gái các ngươi cho con trai họ, và đừng cưới con gái họ cho con trai các ngươi, và đừng bao giờ tìm sự bình an hay sự thịnh vượng của họ, để các ngươi được mạnh mẽ và ăn những sản vật tốt của đất và để lại [đất] làm cơ nghiệp cho con cái các ngươi mãi mãi.'
vi.B: Vậy đừng gả con gái các ngươi cho con trai họ, cũng đừng cưới con gái họ cho con trai các ngươi, và đừng bao giờ tìm cầu sự bình an hay sự thịnh vượng cho họ, để các ngươi được mạnh mẽ, được ăn những sản vật tốt của đất và để lại đất ấy làm cơ nghiệp cho con cháu các ngươi mãi mãi.'
vi.R: Vậy đừng để con gái các ngươi lấy con trai họ, và đừng để con trai các ngươi cưới con gái họ. Đừng bao giờ tìm cách kết thân với họ hay giúp cho họ được thịnh vượng. Như vậy các ngươi sẽ được mạnh mẽ. Các ngươi sẽ được hưởng những sản vật tốt của đất, và để lại đất ấy cho con cháu các ngươi làm sản nghiệp mãi mãi.'

decisions.choice: do not give your daughters ... do not seek their peace or their good: words drawn from Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The ban on marriage repeats Deuteronomy 7:3, and "do not seek their peace or their good" repeats what Deuteronomy 23:7 says of the Ammonites and Moabites. Seeking someone's peace means making treaties and working for their welfare.

decisions.choice: so that you may be strong and possess the land: obedience as the condition of keeping the land
decisions.reason: The law promised that if Israel kept God's commands it would be strong and possess the land and its good things (Deuteronomy 11:8-9). The prayer quotes the promise to show what the people are now putting at risk.

decisions.choice: your children or your sons (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The heirs who inherit the land are the coming generations, sons and daughters both, so Balanced and Readable offer the inclusive word as the default. Literal keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: "hijos", no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already takes in sons and daughters, so the English gender setting on the heirs has no Spanish counterpart (terms note); "su" with ustedes is spanned with its noun where it could be misread.

decisions.choice: "watoto wenu" (B, R) with no gender span; Literal "wana wenu"
decisions.reason: Swahili "watoto" covers sons and daughters, so the inclusive word stands without a setting.

decisions.choice: con cái (Literal), con cháu (Balanced, Readable), no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable use the gender setting for "children / sons". The heirs are sons and daughters both, and Vietnamese "con cái" and "con cháu" already include them, so no span is needed.

source.text: וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ כָּל־הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֔ינוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֨ינוּ֙ הָרָעִ֔ים וּבְאַשְׁמָתֵ֖נוּ הַגְּדֹלָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ חָשַׂ֤כְתָּֽ לְמַ֨טָּה֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וְנָתַ֥תָּה לָּ֛נוּ פְּלֵיטָ֖ה כָּזֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And after all that has come upon us by our evil deeds and by our great guilt, for you, our God, have held back downward from our iniquity and have given us an escaped remnant like this,

en.L: And after all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and because of our great guilt, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, our God, have held back below our iniquities and have given us an escaped remnant such as this,
en.B: After all that has come on us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt, even though {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, our God, have punished us less than our sins deserved and have given us a remnant like this,
en.R: All these troubles came on us because of the evil things we did and because we are so guilty. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, our God, have punished us much less than our sins deserved, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have let some of us survive like this.

es.L: Y después de todo lo que nos ha sobrevenido por nuestras malas obras y por nuestra gran culpa, ya que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Dios nuestro, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} has detenido por debajo de nuestras iniquidades y nos has dado un remanente que escapó como este,
es.B: Después de todo lo que nos ha sucedido por nuestras malas obras y nuestra gran culpa, aunque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Dios nuestro, nos has castigado menos de lo que merecían nuestros pecados y nos has dado un remanente como este,
es.R: Todos estos males nos vinieron por las cosas malas que hicimos y porque somos muy culpables. Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Dios nuestro, nos has castigado mucho menos de lo que merecían nuestros pecados, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has dejado que algunos de nosotros sobrevivamos así.

fr.L: Et après tout ce qui nous est arrivé à cause de nos mauvaises actions et à cause de notre grande culpabilité, puisque {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, notre Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} t’es retenu en dessous de nos iniquités et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as donné un reste de rescapés comme celui-ci,
